blocks.p: A AC1032 drawing, 103.5 MB, exported from Revit. The model spans 42.4 m by 227.0 m and 69.5 m high. Units are millimetres, and every coordinate in this viewer is a model coordinate.
The host file carries 21379 parts. No linked models are attached, so there is no architectural or structural geometry beyond what the host file holds.
28 levels are read from the model's level lines, from B02 at -8,700 mm to L25 at 75,025 mm. The structural grid has 19 lines, used to locate every issue.

The check found 231 major and 432 minor clashes, plus 270 places where surfaces only touch. 565 are measured on the actual intersection solid; 368 involve an open mesh and use the bounding boxes, which overstate the overlap.

Services meet walls or floors at 12 points. 1134 modelled holes and 2 proposed openings are in [[tab:open|Openings]]. Proposed openings are sized to the service plus the clearance and are not approved.

3 rows for proposed openings were added to the schedule. 10 modelled holes matched exactly one existing record by size, service type and material, and 225 have several possible records; all are listed in the reconciliation workbook. Existing records were not changed.
No site setting-out transform: coordinates are model coordinates, not site grid distances.
19 families have no geometry in the exported view and are left out.
1 part far outside the rest of the model, left out of framing: PF-B02-01 (Pipe fitting, 197 m away). Check in Revit.
Opening clearances are provisional: proposed sizes use the default 25 mm for pipes and 50 mm for ducts and tray.
Clash grades are provisional: 25 mm tolerance, not yet confirmed by the project.
3 schedule rows have no level sheet in the template and are listed in the report only.
The DWG was converted with LibreDWG and read with ezdxf. Revit writes each element’s id, type and category on every entity, so plates are grouped by element and classified by category.
Clashes are triangle intersections (FCL through trimesh) between disciplines, level by level. A part fully enclosed inside another without crossing a surface would be missed.
Openings follow the clearance rule and round up to 25 mm. Wall fire ratings and construction come from the model only; where they are missing, the opening is flagged for review.
